statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail eases to 5% in the low band roughly seven and a half hours into the Globex session, with NQ completing a third rotation off its session high inside an unchanged 226-point range.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over 13:00-15:00 UTC, the window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds 30,082.00 (+0.55%) with the 226-point range intact for a third hour; WTI $94.30 and Brent $97.78 extend declines while Hormuz weekend transits fall to 12 - Tail eases to 5%, Stress 31%
body:
A third consecutive hour has now passed without a new session extreme, and that is the substantive change this hour. NQ prints 30,082.00 on Yahoo, up 164.75 points (+0.55%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, stamped 01:16:45 EDT (05:16 UTC). Investing.com shows 30,080.75 at 01:16:56, a 1.25-point spread between two independent feeds. The observed Globex range is unchanged at 29,904.50-30,130.50, so neither a new high nor a new low has printed since roughly 03:15 UTC. Price now sits 48.50 points below the session high, against 46.75 an hour ago, 34 the hour before and 51 before that. The index has therefore rotated off the high, recovered part of the way, and rotated off it again, three times, without extending the envelope in either direction. Three completed rotations inside a fixed 226-point band (0.75%) is sustained, repeated mean reversion - precisely the behaviour this Tail measure is defined against - and no retracement has failed. Tail eases to 5%. It does not go lower because the session's dominant liquidity has not yet arrived and the US cash open is still eight hours away.

Investing.com reports its own day range as 30,079.25-30,090.50 against Yahoo's 29,904.50-30,130.50. That is a session-boundary and sampling convention difference rather than a data conflict: the feeds agree on the last price to within 1.25 points. The wider Globex-session range is the one used here.

The energy complex is holding its decline rather than retracing it. Yahoo's front-month CL=F prints $94.30, down 1.85%, inside a $93.58-$97.03 session range; Brent on BZ=F prints $97.78, down 1.52%, inside $96.98-$100.26. Both are stamped 01:16 EDT. A Reuters report relayed early in the Asian session had crude at its lowest in over a week with Brent near $101.71 and WTI near $98.15; live futures are now roughly four dollars below those levels, so the move has extended rather than reversed. Brent consolidating below $100 instead of snapping back through it is a disinflationary and risk-positive alignment.

One genuinely new piece of evidence arrived this hour, and it cuts against the crude move. Reuters reports weekend vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed to 12 transits from 35 the prior weekend, and the NBC News transit tracker independently confirms throughput nowhere near the hundred-plus ships a day seen before the war. A physical chokepoint tightening while crude sells off is a conflicting signal, not a confirming one, and conflicting signals raise Stress and reduce directional conviction rather than raising Tail. Two further items were verified: a senior Houthi official warned other states against joining Saudi Arabia in renewed Yemen fighting while assuring Washington through Omani mediation that US vessels in the Red Sea would be spared, and Iran's foreign minister departed for New York. Iran has not fired at a host state for nine consecutive days. The diplomatic branch behind the crude move was re-verified at 03:28 UTC: Trump told Fox News he would probably be open to meeting President Pezeshkian, described himself as in deciding mode between pressure, military action and a deal, and Iran has conveyed seven conditions through mediators. A meeting being possible is not a meeting being agreed. The net geopolitical read is de-escalation on the kinetic track, chronic disruption on the physical track, and neither one is an established Tail path.

The rate backdrop is unchanged and remains the heaviest standing weight. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled at least one more this year. The 10-year sits at 5.00% and the 2-year at 4.75% as of the 18 September close; the latest H.15 observation, dated 17 September, reads 4.94% and 4.67%, with an effective funds rate of 3.88%. Kashkari was re-verified this hour from a Reuters syndication: he said on Sunday that inflation is too high in all aspects of the economy and still too high even stripping out energy, and he backed the unanimous hike. That echoes Chair Warsh, who put August PCE near 3.6%. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, and is static while the cash market is shut. The cash reference remains Friday's NDX close of 29,644.17, up 0.67%, set in a tape where the S&P 500 added 0.17% and the Dow shed 0.18% - split internals rather than aligned ones.

Asian cash gives the only live cross-asset confirmation available. Hang Seng trades 24,874.15, up 123.37 points (+0.50%), at 13:11 Hong Kong time - almost exactly the NQ move, constructive without being extended, and a touch softer than an hour ago. Tokyo is closed for Respect for the Aged Day, so the region is running without its largest cash market. The week's principal catalyst was re-verified from source: Bessent and Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng and Li Chenggang in New York on Sunday, Bessent called the talks very successful, the Board of Trade mechanism is operational and targets non-strategic goods, and a working group resumes on Monday. The AI dialogue excludes advanced-chip export controls, and neither critical minerals nor the November 10 truce expiry was addressed. The Trump-Xi summit is confirmed for 24 September in Washington. Monday's own calendar is light and was re-verified: Goolsbee at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and bill auctions at 15:30 UTC. Trading Economics again shows figures in its actual column for releases that have not yet occurred, so no actual value is carried here for them.

The shared Finviz context refreshed during this run and is now inside the freshness bound, though collection status remains partial with the futures and calendar sections failed, so it supplies no cross-asset futures or event data. Its available sections are explicitly latest-session and carry no source as-of, so they describe Friday's cash tape rather than current structure. On that basis the tone is constructive but not aligned: Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%, semiconductors positive in five of seven names with a 1.28% mean but a 3.21% dispersion and QCOM down 5.82%, and megacaps split exactly four up and four down for a 0.24% mean. Split megacap participation is a conflicting reading, which reduces directional conviction rather than amplifying Tail, and it is one reason this assessment carries no breadth amplifier. Its headline section is discovery-only: items describing tech lifting Asian share markets, oil slipping and Brent extending its decline corroborate the independently verified live quotes above, but they were not separately fetched and so are not relied on or cited as verified evidence.

Net: Tail 5%, down one point, because a third completed rotation inside an unchanged range is sustained mean reversion and no retracement has failed. The mapped state stays EA_ON and green. Stress holds at 31%: crude extending its decline and constructive Asian equities pull down, while a newly verified collapse in Hormuz transits conflicting with that crude move, an unchanged 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking hold it up. Confidence rises to 81% on two futures feeds agreeing within 1.25 points at a 05:16 UTC stamp, live WTI and Brent, a live Asian cash index, a re-verified seven-day US calendar and five independently fetched and verified reports including two new this hour, and on a refreshed shared context whose available sections show no aligned breadth amplifier; it is discounted for the absence of live US cash breadth, an H.15 observation dated 17 September, and a shared context that still carries no futures or calendar sections.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime spanning Sunday 20 September and the Globex reopen into Monday. Tail held between 5% and 9% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. It sat flat at 5% for the whole of Sunday through the weekend halt, rose with the reopen as the first live price path formed, peaked at 9% in the 01:00 UTC slot, then eased for three consecutive hours to 6% as that extension unwound. Stress drifted from 28-31% on Sunday into a 32-35% band overnight as the post-hike rate backdrop accumulated, easing to 31% in the final hour. Confidence ranged from 70% to 80%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened and independent feeds could be cross-checked. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment lowers Tail to 5%, a third consecutive decline and the lowest reading since the reopen.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; secondary 10% readings fall on the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release hour and power hour into the 20:00 UTC close. The cycle low of 5% covers the current hour and the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists and a no-retracement trend is mechanically impossible. Stress is projected between 31% and 36%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year, a Fed that has just resumed hiking and a Hormuz chokepoint tightening against falling crude, and capped by WTI and Brent extending their declines, a calm VIX and a constructive US-China preparatory round that continues on Monday. Confidence decays from 81% to 69% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
